newsitem.title: USA: Bank of New York repeats State Street aims.
newsitem.headline: Bank of New York repeats State Street aims.

text.p: A representative of Bank of New York Co Inc came to State Street Corp's annual meeting in Boston on Tuesday and repeated his company's desire to increase its stake in State Street.

Nicholas Silitch, vice president of public relations at Bank of New York, said the bank still wanted to raise its stake in State Street to 9.9 percent from 4.9 percent, despite the Boston bank's opposition and an unfavorable ruling by Massachusetts banking regulators.

"The Bank of New York remains committed to making a 9.9 percent passive investment in State Street," Silitch told the annual meeting. "We regret State Street management's opposition to our proposed investment. We do not understand how it adversely affects the shareholder."
State Street Chief Executive Marshall Carter told reporters later that his bank was committed to remaining independent.
"We don't think our biggest shareholder should be our biggest competitor," he said.
On Monday, Bank of New York said it was filing a suit to invalidate a ruling by the Massachusetts Board of Bank Incorporation that denied its application to increase its investment in State Street.
Earlier Carter rejected suggestions that State Street was for sale despite published reports of overtures from Bank of New York.
On Wednesday, Carter said State Street's earnings were growing 15 percent annually on average, and strong profitability was the best defense against an unwelcome shareholder.
"We believe we have a clear strategic plan in which our board of directors is intimately involved with," he said.

Silitch also told the shareholders that Bank of New York had been opposed to State Street's proposal to drop "Boston" from its name, but as a passive investor, would vote in favor of all of management's proposals.
"We are proud to have included New York in our name," while expanding its global custody business, he said.
Shareholders subsequently approved the bank's plans to change its name to State Street Corp from State Street Boston Corp.
State Street officials said later they were baffled why Bank of New York would state its opposition, and then vote for the name change.
Carter said the long-term goal of State Street, the leader in the market for post-trade securities custodians, will make mergers and acquisitions to compete in pre-trade and trading services.
